proposed: Most reported cases of EOPPC are of serous histology, although nonserous tumors have been observed.
why: Dropped the '(serous surface carcinoma)' label, which no quote states; added the quote's caveat that nonserous tumors have been observed.

proposed: In one report, the median survival time for patients with advanced ovarian cancer was only 3 years.
why: The quote gives a median of 3 years for advanced ovarian cancer; the 'better' and 'up to 2 years' wording contradicts or is unsupported, so it was replaced.

proposed: Chemotherapy-induced N&V is one of the most distressing side effects of cancer treatment, and nausea and vomiting have been described as the most common side effects of chemotherapy.
why: Quote 0 carries 'one of the most distressing' side effects; quote 1 carries 'most common'. 'Acute' is not stated and was dropped.

proposed: In one study, more than half of the patients with moderate to severe pain were nonresponders at the first follow-up.
why: The quote states the more-than-half nonresponder finding at first follow-up; the 1,612 sample, the outpatient setting, and nurse-and-physician care are not stated and were dropped.

proposed: Methadone is a mu-receptor agonist, and some data also indicate that it acts as an antagonist at the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor.
why: Quote 0 states mu-agonism; quote 1 says NMDA antagonism only as 'some data indicate', so that half is hedged.

proposed: Neuropathic cancer pain, which is experienced by 30-40% of patients with cancer, significantly reduces quality of life, and pain is one of the biggest problems in the treatment of cancer patients.
why: Quote 0 covers neuropathic cancer pain only (prevalence and quality of life); quote 1 calls pain one of the biggest problems. 'Most common symptom' and 'functional status' are unsupported.

proposed: Studies have shown that, in patients receiving moderately emetogenic chemotherapy, dexamethasone plus a 5HT3RA improved complete control of vomiting compared with a 5HT3RA alone.
why: The quote supports improved vomiting control in moderately emetogenic chemotherapy; nothing is stated about rescue medications or general patient outcomes.

proposed: In adults with cancer, malnutrition was more common than sarcopenia, and it was associated with a higher mortality risk.
why: Quote 0 gives malnutrition's relative frequency and its link to higher mortality; morbidity and quality of life are linked only to sarcopenia (quote 1), so they were dropped.

proposed: In one study of cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy, the malnutrition screening test (MST) was a more valid screening method than MUST and NRS-2002 for predicting loss of lean mass above 5%, and its routine use was recommended; in another study, NRS-2002 showed greater concordance with GLIM criteria than MST.
why: Quote 0 supports MST validity and recommendation in radiotherapy patients; quote 1 adds a contrary comparison. The two-parameter description is not stated and was dropped.

proposed: Malnutrition, for which tumor subsite is one of the major determinants, is most prevalent in patients with pancreatic, esophageal and other gastroenteric cancers, head and neck cancers, and lung cancers.
why: The quote ranks these cancers highest for malnutrition prevalence; it says nothing on weight loss specifically or on breast or lower gastrointestinal cancers being lower.

proposed: In one study, one in five colorectal cancer survivors showed clinical distress, and in another study 32.1% of cancer survivors had severe or pathological fear of recurrence.
why: Quote 0 gives one in five for colorectal survivors; quote 1 gives 32.1% for severe fear of recurrence. The general one-third figure and the quality-of-life link are not stated.

proposed: Mood disorders are common in patients with cancer: in one study some combination of mood disorders occurred in 30-40% of patients in hospital settings, and in another study 38.2% were classified as depressed and 32.2% as anxious.
why: Both quotes give frequencies of depression, anxiety or mood disorders; post-traumatic stress disorder and the 'manifestations of distress' framing are not stated and were dropped.

proposed: Early palliative care consultation has the potential to decrease costs and length of stay, and in one study consultations in the emergency department had a shorter hospital stay and lower median direct costs for the index hospitalization than consultations on the floor.
why: Quotes support lower costs and shorter stay only; intensive care unit use, emergency department use and readmission are not stated. 'Potential' follows quote 1.

proposed: In their efforts to define the concept of a "Good Death," researchers identified 2,652 titles and, after screening and final selection, narrowed them down to 29 relevant publications for analysis.
why: The quote gives 29 publications retained from 2,652 titles, not 36. The patient-defined parameters detail is not stated and was dropped.

proposed: In one study, patients with HDHP coverage had greater out-of-pocket costs than patients with LDHP coverage, and higher out-of-pocket costs for expensive oral cancer drugs were associated with a greater likelihood of discontinuing or delaying drug therapy.
why: Quote 0 supports greater out-of-pocket costs; quote 1 supports poorer adherence. Financial well-being, quality of life and psychosocial health are not stated and were dropped.

proposed: Hartstein noted that CMS, which is the biggest payer for cancer care in this country, was prohibited from negotiating prices and interfering with the practice of medicine; starting in 2026, Medicare will be able to negotiate drug prices.
why: The quote dates a change: from 2026 Medicare can negotiate drug prices. The prohibition is kept as Hartstein's attributed statement in the past tense.

proposed: When assessed using the ESMO-MCBS, there were no significant associations between monthly treatment costs for solid tumours and clinical benefit in all assessed countries.
why: The quote states the no-association finding specifically for the ESMO-MCBS scale, so the claim is narrowed to that scale.

proposed: But nearly 90 percent of the world's children who develop cancer reside in low-income and middle-income countries.
why: The quote says nearly 90%, not 80%, and names low-income and middle-income countries rather than 'resource-poor' countries.

proposed: Large inequities in cervical cancer currently exist for Indigenous peoples in Australia, Canada, New Zealand and the US.
why: The quote supports cervical cancer inequities for Indigenous peoples in four named countries; lung and liver cancers and the preventable or screening-detectable framing are not stated.

proposed: In one study, APOBEC3B was found to promote chromosomal instability early in cancer evolution through DNA replication stress.
why: The quote links early chromosomal instability to replication stress specifically via APOBEC3B in one study, not as the general cause.

proposed: Replication stress can lead to the collapse of replication forks into one-ended DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs).
why: The quote says replication stress triggers fork collapse to one-ended double-strand breaks; 'prolonged' is not stated and was dropped.

proposed: Activated p53 induces cell cycle arrest, DNA repair or apoptosis, and one of the genes it activates is an inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases.
why: Quote 0 gives arrest, repair or apoptosis; quote 1 gives an activated CDK inhibitor. p21, the G1-S checkpoint and the 'if damage is irreparable' condition are not named in the quotes.

proposed: For human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, the KRAS oncogene is present in over 90% of cases, and its mutation is most frequently one of three gain-of-function substitutions of codon 12 glycine.
why: The quote supports codon 12 gain-of-function substitutions in over 90% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas; the valine and aspartate substitutions are not named and were dropped.

proposed: In some diseases both alleles of a gene need to be mutated: in one disease mutations in both alleles of the gene are required for development, although carriers of monoallelic mutations have an increased risk of colorectal cancer, and loss of the tumour suppressors TP53 and RB1 is obligatory in SCLC.
why: Quote 0 states a both-allele requirement for one disease only; quote 1 states TP53 and RB1 loss is obligatory in SCLC only. The general rule is not stated.

proposed: In particular, genomic profiling of SCLC shows that the tumour suppressor gene RB1 is almost always functionally inactivated, together with TP53.
why: The quote supports RB1 inactivation in SCLC only; bladder and breast carcinomas are not stated.

proposed: TP53 is the most frequently mutated gene in human cancers.
why: The quote says TP53 is the most frequently mutated gene in human cancers; the 'up to 50%' figure is not stated and was dropped.

proposed: The protein p21 is involved in p53-mediated inhibition of cellular proliferation in response to DNA damage, and its binding to CDK2 leads to CDK2/cyclin E inactivation at the G1-S DNA damage checkpoint, arresting cells at the G1-S transition.
why: Quote 0 links p21 to p53-mediated inhibition; quote 1 gives G1-S arrest via CDK2. That p53 upregulates p21 expression is not stated, so it was dropped.

proposed: The concept of tumor suppression was further solidified by a statistical analysis of retinoblastoma, which provided the first evidence that tumorigenesis can be initiated by as few as two mutations and founded the "two-hit hypothesis."
why: The quote credits a statistical analysis of retinoblastoma with founding the two-hit hypothesis; Knudson is not named, so the name was dropped.

proposed: DNA damage is sensed by kinases such as ATR, a serine/threonine protein kinase that acts as a DNA damage sensor and activates checkpoint signaling upon genotoxic stresses, including DNA replication stalling.
why: The quote names ATR as a DNA damage sensor; ATM and the 'complexes' wording are not stated and were dropped.

proposed: One study found that loss of the Y chromosome correlates with poor prognosis in patients with bladder cancer, and that Y-negative tumours showed an increased response to anti-PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade therapy in both mice and patients with cancer.
why: Both quotes concern loss of Y only: prognosis in bladder cancer and anti-PD-1 response. General chromosome abnormalities and chemotherapy response are not covered.

proposed: Bloom syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding a DNA helicase of the RecQ type.
why: The quote states autosomal recessive inheritance and mutation in the gene encoding a DNA helicase; the BLM name and the 'lack of BLM helicase enzyme' mechanism are not stated.

proposed: It has been suggested that an early chromosomal change, the Ph translocation, might be a first event to immortalize cell proliferation.
why: The quote supports only a hedged suggestion about the Ph translocation as a first event; the general multistep-progression claim is not stated.

proposed: Chromosome 1 abnormalities are frequent in breast carcinomas: cytogenetic markers involving the long arm of chromosome 1 are the most frequently observed karyotypic changes in breast cancer, and in one study involvement of a region on the short arm reached 73%.
why: Replaced 'most breast carcinomas' with what the quotes state: long arm changes are the most frequent karyotypic change (quote 1) and 73% short arm involvement in one study (quote 0).

proposed: Numerical chromosome abnormalities, mainly including aneuploidy and chromosome instability, are caused by chromosome segregation errors in mitosis, whereas a major source of structural chromosome abnormalities is replication stress.
why: Quote 0 supports the numerical half; quote 1 attributes structural aberrations to replication stress, not DNA damage generally. The focal or arm-level gain-or-loss detail is not stated.

proposed: The Philadelphia chromosome is found in some leukemias, including acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL).
why: The quote only names Philadelphia chromosome-positive ALL; CML as hallmark and AML, CNL and MPAL are not covered.

proposed: Theodor Boveri hypothesized over a century ago that numerical aneuploidy, which can result from failures in accurate chromosome segregation during mitosis, promotes tumorigenesis.
why: The quote credits Boveri with a century-old hypothesis that aneuploidy promotes tumorigenesis; 'first proposed' and 'chromosomal abnormalities in general' are not stated.

proposed: ATM kinase acts as a DNA damage sensor that activates checkpoint signaling upon double strand breaks.
why: The quote supports ATM sensing double strand breaks and activating checkpoint signaling; homologous recombination, non-homologous end joining and cancer prevention are not stated and were dropped.

proposed: Mutations in many homologous-recombination genes lead to cancer predisposition, and mutations in DNA excision repair genes are associated with progeroid syndromes.
why: Quote 0 links many HR gene mutations to cancer predisposition; quote 1 links excision repair gene mutations to progeroid syndromes. The count 'at least 30' is not stated.

proposed: Mutations in the MLH1 gene are frequently found in hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer (HNPCC).
why: The quote supports MLH1 as a locus frequently mutated in HNPCC; MSH2, MSH6, PMS2, ovarian cancer and the Lynch syndrome synonym are not stated.

proposed: The ATM kinase acts as a DNA damage sensor that activates checkpoint signaling upon double strand breaks (DSBs), and it phosphorylates many downstream proteins, including CHEK2, p53 and BRCA1.
why: Quote 0 supports DSB sensing and checkpoint signaling; quote 1 lists downstream substrates. 'Early, pivotal' and 'transducer and effector' wording are not stated and were dropped.
Quote 0 states a small number of frequently altered genes and a much larger number of infrequently altered genes; the claim is that in substance, with only a wording difference.

proposed: The gene ABL1, located on chromosome 9, has been found fused to a variety of translocation partner genes in various leukemias, most notably BCR in the t(9;22) translocation.
why: Dropped 'always'; quote 1 gives fusion with BCR in t(9;22) among many partners, and quote 0 gives the chromosome 9 location. The mouse viral oncogene precursor is not stated.

proposed: In 1911, Peyton Rous described a curious observation, later explained by a virus named for him, that led to the discovery of oncogenes.
why: The quote supports Rous's 1911 observation and the virus named for him; the 1908 avian erythroblastosis virus and the chicken fibrosarcoma isolation are not stated.

proposed: In one study, provirus integrations ranged from 217 to 2,584 bp upstream of the TERT transcription initiation site and were all in the opposite orientation to TERT, whereas proviruses integrated on the 3' side of a gene are usually in the same transcriptional orientation.
why: Quote 0 gives upstream integrations in the opposite orientation; quote 1 gives usual same orientation on the 3' side. 'Broad range' and 'many loci' are not stated.

proposed: Later identified as the shortened chromosome 22 produced by a reciprocal translocation that also lengthens chromosome 9, this abnormality was designated the Philadelphia chromosome.
why: The quote states the Philadelphia chromosome arises from a reciprocal translocation giving a lengthened chromosome 9 and a shortened chromosome 22; the naming after its city of discovery is not stated.

proposed: HTLV-1 is the only identified oncogenic human retrovirus and is the infectious cause of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma.
why: The quote names HTLV-1 as the only identified oncogenic human retrovirus causing adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma; hairy cell leukemia and animal cancers are not stated.

proposed: Avian retroviruses have obtained their transforming sequences from chicken cellular DNA by recombination.
why: The quote says avian retroviruses obtained transforming sequences from chicken cellular DNA; RSV, src and 'first' are not stated and were dropped.

proposed: Using DNA transfection analysis on NIH 3T3 cells, activated human oncogenes have been isolated from a variety of fresh solid tumours, and many cellular oncogenes have been identified in human cancerous cells by DNA transfection.
why: Both quotes support oncogene identification by DNA transfection; isolating and sequencing transferred DNA fragments is not stated and was dropped.

proposed: Studies revealed that the v-Src oncogene, a transmissible agent responsible for tumorigenesis in chickens, has a cellular homologue.
why: The quote establishes a cellular homologue of v-Src; that v-src is a captured and altered cellular gene is not stated and was dropped.

proposed: The ABL1 gene has been found fused to a variety of translocation partner genes in various leukemias, most notably in the t(9;22) translocation, which results in a fusion with the 5' end of the breakpoint cluster region gene (BCR).
why: The quote states ABL1 fuses with the 5' end of BCR in t(9;22); the resulting fusion protein and its composition are not described, so those were dropped.

proposed: An important finding was that normal eukaryotic cells contain gene sequences that are highly homologous to oncogenes but do not cause neoplastic transformation.
why: The quote states normal cells contain oncogene-homologous sequences; the 'viral' counterpart discovery and 'truly revolutionary' framing are not stated.

proposed: The ret proto-oncogene can undergo oncogenic activation through both cytogenetic rearrangement and activating point mutations.
why: The quote supports activating point mutations in the ret proto-oncogene; its tie to MEN2A is not stated in the text and was dropped.

proposed: RAS genes are the most frequently mutated oncogene family in human cancer, and in some cancers, such as pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, the KRAS mutation frequency is near 100%.
why: Quote 1 gives RAS as the most frequently mutated oncogene family; quote 0 gives near 100% KRAS in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. The 15% overall and 90% figures are not stated.

proposed: The KRAS gene is mutated in many human cancers: 23% of adult pan-cancer samples had KRAS alterations, of which 88% were mutations, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma has a near 100% KRAS mutation frequency.
why: Quote 1 gives the pan-cancer figure; quote 0 gives near 100% in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. The lung (a quarter) and colon (half) figures are not stated and were dropped.

proposed: In human bladder carcinoma cell lines EJ and T24, a transforming gene closely related to the v-Ha-ras oncogene of the rat-derived Harvey sarcoma virus was cloned, and a single point mutation distinguishes it from the normal human homologue (c-Ha-ras1) and is thought to be solely responsible for its transforming potential.
why: The quote describes one single-point-mutation difference between a transforming ras gene and its normal homologue in two cell lines; a general 'essentially identical' retroviral comparison is not stated.

proposed: In neuroblastoma, amplification of the MYC family member MYCN is found in about 25% of cases and correlates with high-risk disease and poor prognosis.
why: The quote gives MYCN amplification in about 25% of cases with poor prognosis; 'often', large amounts of myc protein and 'childhood tumor' are not stated.

proposed: Members of the Ras oncogene family are related to the transforming genes of mammalian sarcoma retroviruses.
why: The quote states the Ras family is related to transforming genes of mammalian sarcoma retroviruses; the Harvey and Kirsten names, progenitor status, and mouse and rat are not stated.

proposed: One analysis found that approximately 19% of patients with cancer harbor Ras mutations, equivalent to approximately 3.4 million new cases per year worldwide.
why: The quote gives about 19%, not 30%, of patients with cancer harboring Ras mutations. The claim about how Ras was first discovered is not stated and was dropped.

proposed: Imatinib (Gleevec) received its original approval on 10 May 2001.
why: The record only shows the original approval of Gleevec dated 2001-05-10. 'First tyrosine kinase inhibitor' and the leukemia indication are not stated and were dropped.

proposed: MYC functions as a transcription factor that binds DNA and activates the transcription of growth-related genes.
why: The quote states MYC is a transcription factor activating growth-related genes; its oncogene-class status and the cell cycle and metabolism roles are not stated.

proposed: Studies indicated that nonhereditary retinoblastoma is mainly caused by inactivation of both RB1 alleles at a somatic level.
why: The quote states both RB1 alleles are inactivated in nonhereditary retinoblastoma; gene-mapping studies and the tumor-suppressor framing are not stated.
